newsitem.title: USA: Court rules on Country World claims hearing.
newsitem.headline: Court rules on Country World claims hearing.

text.p: Holly Products Inc said on Friday that a U.S. Bankruptcy Court ruled that its Country World Casinos Inc unit had to pay eight percent interest on an unpaid balance due TommyKnocker Casino Corp/New Allied Development Corp.

Country World bought land from TommyKnocker/New Allied to build a casino, Holly Products said. Country World said it stopped making mortgage payments on the property because TommyKnocker/New Allied had not paid off the first lien.
Holly Products said it took Country World into Chapter 11 under U.S. bankruptcy law to protect the property.
But a U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Boulder ruled that Country World did not have to repay debt at an 18 percent default interest rate, Holly Products said.

The court said each party had to pay their own legal fees, the company said. It also found Country World Casinos was not in default of its agreement with TommyKnocker/New Allied Development with regard to filing a registration for its preferred stock, Holly Products said.
Until TommyKnocker/New Allied filed such a registration statement and Country World failed to pay for the cost, Country World was not in breach of the agreement, Holly said.
Finally, Holly said the court upheld TommyKnocker/New Allied's claim that Country World was not entitled to an offset on the environmental clean-up, as the work had been completed.
